title: Worst-case-ratio framing note for quantum optimization: beating GW / basic-SDP thresholds now implies NP in BQP
summary: The direct Max-Cut theorem and the Unique Games Theorem give deterministic poly-time Karp reductions, so any poly-time quantum algorithm with worst-case (or expected) ratio > 0.8786 on Max-Cut, or above Raghavendra's SDP threshold on any Max-CSP, would put NP in BQP with no UGC caveat. Quantum-optimization papers and vendors should stop using GW's worst-case ratio as a target and benchmark instance-wise against GW+local search and class-specific classical baselines (e.g. 0.9326 on cubic graphs).
beneficiaries: Quantum-optimization benchmarking groups (QAOA, annealing, Ising machines), referees, vendor technical marketing, Qiskit Optimization docs users
first_step: Draft a 2-3 page note covering Max-Cut/Max-CSP (rows 1-4 of the claim table) citing thm:gap and OptimalMaxCut.lean; open a one-line docs PR on the Qiskit GW docstring.
measurement: Share of new QAOA/annealing papers that make unqualified 'beats GW' claims; acceptance of the docs PR; citations of the note.
risks: Unreviewed (mitigated: top-line Lean-formalized, 0 sorry in solution tree, not built by us). Marginal: UGC was widely assumed. Does not constrain average-case, instance-specific, restricted-class or super-polynomial-time claims.

title: Quantum Max-Cut UG-hardness becomes NP-hardness (product-state 0.9859; 0.956 modulo vector-Borell)
summary: Hwang-Neeman-Parekh-Thompson-Wright and arXiv:2306.03912 prove Quantum Max-Cut approximation hardness under UGC; if their parameter order matches thm:ugc (errors fixed before alphabet), the hypothesis can be replaced by P != NP. The 0.956 bound still needs the vector-valued Borell conjecture.
beneficiaries: Quantum Hamiltonian-complexity / approximation theorists; survey authors
first_step: Ask the HNPTW authors (or a UG expert) to confirm the quantifier compatibility; update survey tables accordingly.
measurement: Written confirmation; updated statements in follow-up papers/surveys.
risks: Quantifier mismatch (e.g. need for strong/left-regular UG) could block direct transfer; low practical stakes.

title: Retire the 'GBS counts perfect matchings faster than classical' complexity claim
summary: Approximate counting of perfect matchings in arbitrary unweighted graphs (and polynomially bounded nonnegative integer weights via path gadgets) now has a classical FPRAS, while the GBS all-ones-event estimator of Bradler et al. 2018 needs exponentially many samples in general; the complexity-theoretic advantage is reversed. Practically nothing changes (exact O(n^3 2^{n/2}) counting beats the galactic FPRAS below n ~ 2.8e5).

targets.name: The Walrus docs: approximate PM-counting methods

beneficiaries: GBS applications researchers (Xanadu, USTC Jiuzhang groups), quantum-advantage reviewers
first_step: Write a short comment/blog post on the PM-counting claim citing thm:main and the cost table; optional one-sentence docs PR to The Walrus algorithms.rst.
measurement: Docs PR merged; the claim no longer repeated in new GBS-application papers.
risks: FPRAS unreviewed; Lean doc describes a formalization (MatchingCount, 0 sorry) but the catalogue/formalization.yaml do not list it.

title: Ideal unweighted-graph GBS sampling is classically poly-time in principle (ladder-graph reduction + FPRAS + JVV)
summary: We verified exactly that sum_S x^{|S|} prod_{v not in S} r_v Haf(A_S)^2 = Haf(ladder), where the ladder is two copies of G joined by rungs; hence the collision-free lossless PNR GBS law Pr(S) ∝ x^{|S|} Haf(A_S)^2 on an unweighted graph is a perfect-matching marginal of an explicit graph, and the 113 FPRAS + its JVV deletion sampler give a classical poly-time approximate sampler, removing the obstacle (non-bipartite PM sampling) that limited Zhang et al. 2025 to dense graphs. A note should extend this to collision patterns and node weights and state precisely which GBS-application hardness arguments lose their basis.
beneficiaries: GBS complexity theorists and applications community; quantum-advantage assessments
first_step: Write up the ladder identity (scratch_qadvantage/gbs_ladder_identity.py), extend to collisions (vertex blow-up) and WAW node weights, and circulate to Quesada/Oh/Li groups.
measurement: Acceptance as a note/preprint; citations in GBS-application papers; whether any remaining application claims are restated in terms of lossy/threshold/complex settings.
risks: May be folklore; inherits galactic degree (~6,500) so zero practical impact; collision/threshold-detector (Torontonian) and lossy cases not covered.

title: Time-to-epsilon benchmark for SK / large-girth Max-Cut: QAOA vs now-unconditional IAMP/EAMS and heuristics
summary: 281's companion (independently Chen 2026) makes the El Alaoui-Montanari-Sellke message-passing optimizer unconditional (C(eps) n^2 operations), so 'p=11 QAOA beats every unconditional classical algorithm' is obsolete and any QAOA advantage on SK can only lie in epsilon-scaling, which neither side has bounded. Our quick experiment shows 3 s of single-core SA at n=1000 matches infinite-size QAOA depth p~240 (~1.2e8 ZZ gates per shot). A public time-to-epsilon benchmark (QAOA p(eps) from QOKit tables vs IAMP vs SA/PT) would settle the remaining claim.
beneficiaries: JPMC/Argonne, MIT, Google QAOA groups; quantum-optimization advantage assessors; funders
first_step: Implement IAMP for SK with a numerically solved zero-temperature Parisi gamma; reproduce energy-vs-time at n=1e3-1e4 alongside SA and QOKit's QAOA p(eps) fit (P*-v_p ~ 0.93 p^-0.84).
measurement: Fitted classical time-to-(1-eps) exponents vs QAOA's eps^-1.13 depth scaling; full gate-count vs wall-clock comparison table.
risks: IAMP numerics near t->1 delicate; finite-n optima below P*; SA has no guarantee; extrapolation of QAOA beyond p=80.

title: Architecture note: native multi-controlled (C^kZ) gates cannot give constant-depth GHZ/fanout/parity
summary: In the model of one-qubit gates plus layers of product-state reflections (covering Rydberg C^kZ/C^kX in any local basis), constant-depth poly-size circuits cannot compute parity or prepare GHZ-like (felinity) or Dicke states for large n. Resource estimates and architecture comparisons should budget log depth, measurement+feedforward, or a fanout/global gate; no explicit n0 is given.

targets.name: QOKit dicke_simple (linear-depth Dicke prep in use)

beneficiaries: Neutral-atom and ion architecture teams; compiler/resource-estimation authors
first_step: Add one paragraph to the qadvantage-1 note mapping thm:parity/cor:state-preparation onto native gate sets (multi-control vs multi-target/global vs dynamic circuits).
risks: Asymptotic only; excludes measurement+feedforward and fanout gates, which practice already uses; nobody currently plans constant-depth GHZ from C^kZ.

title: Cite continuum (proton-only) QMA-hardness in quantum-chemistry advantage assessments
summary: Ground-state energy estimation for the full 3D continuum electronic Hamiltonian with unit-charge nuclei is QMA-hard under deterministic Karp reductions, closing the finite-basis loophole in O'Gorman et al. 2022. Generic 'quantum computers will solve chemistry' claims would imply QMA in BQP; advantage claims must name the structural assumption (guided state overlap, gap path). Real molecules are unaffected.
beneficiaries: Quantum-chemistry advantage assessors, resource-estimation authors, science journalists
first_step: Include one paragraph and citation in the qadvantage-1 note; suggest the citation to authors of chemistry-advantage reviews.
risks: Consensus already expected this; instances are polynomially stretched H clusters with unspecified large exponents; QMA membership not asserted.

title: Provable exp(O~(L)) algorithm for frustrated, globally gapped 2D ground states (2D analogue of LVV, subexponential)
summary: The 2D area law and polynomial PEPS are existence-only, and polynomial-time algorithms for the class are ruled out unless NP=RP (Abrahamsen 2020's classical unique-SAT instances are in the class). A meaningful follow-on is a subexponential exp(O~(sqrt n)) search algorithm matching the existence-level snake-MPS bound; the obvious AGSP route via prop:positive is circular because its centering needs the ground-state local energies.
beneficiaries: Hamiltonian-complexity theorists; long-run justification for 2D DMRG/PEPS practice
first_step: Check whether the collar/information estimates plus a bootstrapped local-energy estimate yield an exp(O~(L)) RRG-style search on L x L grids.
measurement: A theorem with explicit runtime; no practical benchmark expected.
risks: Long, unrefereed, unformalized proofs; unspecified large exponent c; may be no easier than the frustration-free case already solved.

title: DO NOT: implement the general-graph FPRAS for hafnian / GBS benchmarking
summary: Transcribing the paper's explicit parameters gives at least 10^13155 chain steps at n=10 and 10^20792 at n=144; effective degree ~6,500; it beats exact O(n^3 2^{n/2}) only beyond n~2.8e5 where both cost ~10^42519. Galactic: zero practical value.

title: DO NOT: use the 281 construction for QAOA angle/depth schedules or cite it as evidence of QAOA speedup
summary: The theorem is existential in the thermodynamic-first limit with no depth bound and a word containing seed simulations, echoes, inverse and very large angles; numerically optimized QOKit angles dominate. It proves only that QAOA reaches what the (now unconditional) classical O(n^2) algorithm reaches, so it cannot support a polynomial-in-n speedup claim.

title: DO NOT: build a polynomial-time 2D gapped ground-state solver (classical or quantum) on the area law / PEPS existence
summary: The theorem's hypothesis class contains classical frustration-free gap-1 unique-ground-state planar 3SAT encodings, so poly-time ground-state finding is NP-hard under randomized reductions (Abrahamsen 2020); neither classical nor quantum poly-time is possible unless NP in RP / BQP. The area law changes representability only; the exponent c gives no bond-dimension guidance.
risks: Claims that '2D gapped is classically easy' would be wrong.

title: DO NOT: feed exact factoring (279), oracle unitary synthesis (283) or the quartic separation (284) into roadmaps, compilers or resource estimates
summary: 279's polynomials are explicitly not practical and Las Vegas Shor/Gidney-style estimates are unaffected; 283 needs a target-dependent oracle of unrestricted size and achieves only diamond error 1/2; 284 shows R=O(Q^4) is tight only for contrived pointer/cheat-sheet total functions, changing no practical speedup analysis.

title: DO NOT: change QAOA-on-LABS benchmarks because of unbounded merit factors (076); only fix 'asymptotically constant' wording
summary: Max merit factor -> infinity is non-constructive with no rate; LABS time-to-exact-optimum benchmarks at N<=40-66 (QOKit, Shaydulin et al. 2024) are untouched. Only motivating text that says the asymptotic merit factor stays approximately constant should be corrected (can be folded into the qadvantage-1 note).

title: DO NOT: use the QAC0 parity bound (274) as a concrete depth lower bound in compilers at n~10-1000
summary: The theorem holds only for all sufficiently large n at fixed depth with no explicit threshold, and excludes measurement+feedforward and fanout-type gates that hardware already uses; it cannot certify any concrete depth for real devices.
risks: Misapplied lower bounds in architecture comparisons.
